sentences.text: The petitioners have filed the present Writ Petition seeking for issuance of writ of certiorari to quash the endorsement at Annexure-'D' dated 18.12.2008, whereby the request of petitioners has been rejected, while observing that during the relevant period of time, there were no Rules for allotment of alternative sites.
The petitioners have sought for consequential relief of issuance of writ of mandamus to direct the respondent No.2 to allot alternative sites to the petitioners.

2. It is to be noticed that during an earlier point of time, W.P.No.10420/2006 (BDA) came to be filed by the petitioners seeking a direction to the respondent- Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) to carve a layout in the existing 30 guntas of land at Syed Sab Palya and to allot sites to the petitioners and to direct the respondents to pay compensation of Rs.20.00 lakhs to each of the petitioners towards compensation for having illegally demolished the houses of the petitioners.
Said matter was NC: 2023:KHC:23730 considered and the Writ Petition was disposed off as per the order dated 05.12.2006.

The Court has observed unambiguously that the prayer relating to carving out of layout in the existing 30 guntas of Syed Sab layout and allotting sites to the petitioners and the prayer relating to direction to the respondents to pay compensation of Rs.20.00 lakh each towards the illegal demolition were rejected.

The Court has observed that, as the entire 10 acres of land was put to use and the layout had already come about in the acquired land, the question of considering the prayers referred to above in the said Writ Petition did not arise.

3. The Court has also observed that the question of granting compensation in the form of damages could not be granted in a petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, as it would require evidence.
However, the Court as regards prayer (a) relating to issuance of direction to the respondent-BDA to allot alternative sites to the petitioners

had considered the NC:
2023:KHC:23730 same and an order was passed directing the respondent- BDA to consider the representation in accordance with law.
4. Further, a subsequent round of litigation also came up before this Court in W.P.No.5480/2007,
wherein the prayer sought was to quash the auction sale notification dated 24.03.2007 as regards to the land, which is the subject matter of the writ petition.

This Court disposed off the said Writ Petition by order dated 03.04.2007 reiterating that the only relief the petitioners could seek was to consider the representation that was directed to be considered at an earlier point of time in W.P.No.10420/2006 expeditiously.
5. It is made out from the facts that the endorsement dated 18.12.2008 has been issued by the respondent-BDA in compliance with the direction passed by this Court in W.P.No.5480/2007.

The said endorsement makes a mention regarding the acquisition notification for Nagarabhavi 1st Stage passed on 16.08.1985 including an extent of 10 acres 23 guntas in - 10 - Allabakash vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165830345/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:23730 Survey No.102.

sentences.text: Further, it is pointed out that the Award was approved on 28.01.1987 and the compensation was deposited with the Tahsildar insofar as the extent of Kharab land was concerned.
Insofar as the compensation for the remaining land, the same was deposited with the Civil Court.
The notification under Section 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is also stated to have been passed.

The Authority has observed that, for the relevant period of time, there is no provision under the relevant Rules for considering the allotment of alternative sites and accordingly, by the said endorsement, has rejected the representation of the petitioners.
6. Having heard both sides, it is clear that the petitioners have come to the logical end of their litigation journey.

Despite efforts and directions by this Court for consideration of their representations for allotment of alternative sites, it is the stand taken by the respondent BDA as per their endorsement that there were no Rules permitting them to accommodate such consideration as - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:23730 directed by this Court.

In the absence of any statutory Schemes or Rules for allotment of alternative sites, this Court does not have the residuary power to enlarge substantive consideration of the petitioners' representations.
7. Accordingly, this Court does find any ground made out for interference in the present petition and the petition is liable to be rejected.

Having rejected the challenge to the endorsement, however, it is observed that insofar as the compensation for 23 guntas of Kharab land stated to have been deposited with the Tahsildar, it is open for the petitioners to make their claim for disbursal of the said amount, which the Tahsildar may consider and pass appropriate orders expeditiously and in accordance with law.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner makes a plea that insofar as the compensation that has been deposited if it were to be capable of enhancement, necessary proceedings would be initiated.
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:23730 9.
As regards such submission, it is always open for the petitioners and other persons interested to take appropriate steps in accordance with law, as is permissible.
Accordingly, the petition is disposed off.
